public_rationale: The accessible accounts show reservations about how dramatic GPT-5 would feel and whether it would justify its cost. They also describe expected improvements. That does not clearly establish the stronger statement that prospective customers expected no significant jump. The linked English report could not be verified through read_page, and later GPT-5 performance would not settle what customers believed in 2024.
limitations: The central adjective, significant, has no stated threshold.
The available contemporary account is derivative; the readable Business Insider edition appeared after the target period.
The assessment addresses the factual customer-expectations component, not the rhetorical description of OpenAI’s needs.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI desperately needs something new. It needs something that will show both investors and the media that it is building something meaningful, and while it’s possible it will be able to deliver GPT-5 (their next model) in the near-term future, even potential customers don’t believe the jump will be significant from current model GPT-4.

from_speaker: it’s possible it will be able to deliver GPT-5
even potential customers don’t believe the jump will be significant
our_interpretation: The checkable core is prospective customers’ contemporary expectations, not GPT-5’s eventual performance.
The plain reading is that identifiable prospective customers expected no substantial practical improvement over GPT-4. This does not require unanimity.
The language about desperately needing something meaningful is evaluative framing. The possible near-term release is not a firm forecast.
For this ongoing observation, use July 2024 through the post date: the immediately preceding month and the elapsed portion of August. Customer expectations have no quarterly reporting cycle.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable contemporary customer statements clearly express an expectation that GPT-5 would offer no substantial practical improvement over GPT-4.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records show that the customers invoked as evidence actually expected substantial practical improvements, and that their reservations concerned something else, such as price or whether the advance would equal the previous generational leap.
